title: Extension of a balanced action to the direct-image structure algebra
statement: Let A and B be commutative rings in Type u with an A-algebra structure on B, f:X -> Spec A a scheme morphism [def-pc-scheme], and M a quasi-coherent O_X-module [pqf-def-coherent, def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category]. Let rho:B -> End_(O_X)(M) be a unital ring map satisfying rho(algebraMap(a)) = multiplication by f-sharp(a) for all a in A. Let Y = X times_(Spec A) Spec B [def-pc-fibre-product], pi:Y -> X and fB:Y -> Spec B be its projections. Put C = pi_* O_Y and let S be restriction of module scalars along O_X -> C. Then there is a sheaf G of C-modules and an O_X-linear isomorphism e:M -> S(G) such that for each b in B, open U in X and x in M(U), e_U(rho(b)_U(x)) = (fB-sharp(b) restricted to pi-inverse(U)) acting on e_U(x), with the action taken in G(U). No O_Y-module, quasi-coherence over C, or equivalence is part of this conclusion.

source.document: Stacks Project, Morphisms and Constructions of Schemes
source.place: Tags 01LX (2)-(3), 01SB, and Tag 0897 relative-spectrum paragraph; https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/01LX, https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/01SB and https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/0897 read on 2026-10-13. The local extension of a balanced action is the explicit affine tensor-product construction underlying that paragraph.

proof.text: On an affine open U = Spec C, put N = M(U). Each rho(b) is C-linear; its additivity, multiplicativity and unit come from the ring map rho. The scalar condition identifies the A-actions. Thus the commuting C and B actions extend uniquely to the C tensor_A B action (c tensor b)n = c rho(b)n. On a basic open D(c), quasi-coherence identifies sections with localization, and naturality of rho makes that identification B-linear.

Relative-spectrum base change identifies the direct-image algebra of pi with f-star B-tilde. On U its sections are C tensor_A B and fB-sharp(b) is 1 tensor b. The actions from the preceding step commute with restrictions on the affine basis; refining overlaps by basic affine opens and the sheaf axiom extend them uniquely to all opens. This yields G over pi-star O_Y, with the same underlying abelian sheaf and the original O_X scalar action. The identity on that sheaf gives e. The equality for b holds on the affine basis and hence on all opens. No quasi-coherence assertion over the larger algebra, inverse correspondence, or O_Y-module F is asserted here.

theorem balancedAction_directImage_module
    {A B : Type u} [CommRing A] [CommRing B] [Algebra A B]
    {X : Scheme.{u}} (f : X ⟶ Spec (.of A))
    (M : X.Modules) (hM : M.IsQuasicoherent)
    (rho : B →+* End M)
    (hscalar : ∀ a : A, rho (algebraMap A B a) =
      M.smulHom (((Scheme.ΓSpecIso (.of A)).inv ≫ f.appTop).hom a)) :
    let g := Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom (algebraMap A B))
    let Y := pullback f g
    let pi : Y ⟶ X := pullback.fst f g
    let fB : Y ⟶ Spec (.of B) := pullback.snd f g
    let C := (TopCat.Sheaf.pushforward CommRingCat.{u} pi.base).obj Y.sheaf
    let R := (sheafCompose _ (forget₂ CommRingCat.{u} RingCat.{u})).obj C
    let S := SheafOfModules.restrictScalars.{u}
      ((sheafCompose _ (forget₂ CommRingCat.{u} RingCat.{u})).map
        (show X.sheaf ⟶ C from ⟨pi.c⟩))
    ∃ (G : SheafOfModules.{u} R) (e : M ≅ S.obj G),
      ∀ (b : B) (U : X.Opens) (x : M.val.obj (op U)),
        (e.hom.val.app (op U)).hom ((rho b).val.app (op U) x) =
          Y.presheaf.map (homOfLE (le_top (a := pi ⁻¹ᵁ U))).op
            (((Scheme.ΓSpecIso (.of B)).inv ≫ fB.appTop).hom b) •
              (show G.val.obj (op U) from (e.hom.val.app (op U)).hom x)
